rubric.instructions: You are reviewing rendered pixels from the Stage 3 exact-CUHK scientific layout integration deck. Judge each content page independently at item/page level. PASS for an item only if the visible page reaches a mature doctoral research-group meeting or strong conference-talk bar for its page job. Check that the CUHK Beamer identity is visible; the main scientific object is prominent and projection-readable; math is genuinely typeset rather than source-like text; result figures use readable native axes, ticks, facets, method legend, nominal line, and callout; experiment design shows typed hierarchy, DGP factors, procedures, endpoints, and directional scientific relations; medical comparison uses same-case ROI crop/zoom imagery with adjacent TP/FP/FN legend; discussion/next-experiment content shows evidence-to-decision research reasoning rather than generic future-work boxes. Mark REVISE for any page that looks like a generic card/dashboard/box-arrow fixture, has internal provenance or QA language, has source-like math, hides the evidence in a tiny figure, clips content, uses meaningless whitespace, or repeats one template face without scientific specificity. Top-level PASS means all six content items pass; top-level REVISE if any item has a blocking visual maturity issue. Do not infer quality from filenames, hashes, metadata, or presumed provenance; inspect the actual pixels.
source_contracts: Stage 2 gold/reference pixels are evidence only and are not runtime assets.
This is a Stage 3 engineering integration deck, not a final real-paper holdout.

observations: Purple navigation band and consistent academic slide styling are visible.
The centered mixed-effects model is genuinely typeset, large, and projection-readable.
The accompanying ICC relation is typeset and directly explains the model implication.
item_reviews.summary: A clean model page with the mathematical object as the dominant visible evidence.

observations: The coverage figure has three readable G facets, native axes and ticks, a labeled 0.95 nominal line, two method series, and a method key.
The small-G callout directly points to the cluster-robust estimate.
Captions and takeaway text explain the figure without obscuring it.
item_reviews.summary: A readable multi-facet result figure with visible comparison, reference line, and interpretation.

observations: The page visibly sequences DGP stress factors, nested center hierarchy, interval procedures, and endpoints with directional connectors.
DGP factors include centers, ICC values, and cluster balance; the hierarchy and repeated-replicate procedure are explicitly shown.
Endpoint labels cover coverage target, interval width, and treatment-effect bias.
item_reviews.summary: The experiment design is scientifically specific and visibly encodes the generation-to-estimation-to-evaluation relation.

observations: The negative-evidence bar chart has native y-axis ticks, method colors, error bars, labeled values, and a visible 0.95 target line.
The high-ICC cluster-robust result is explicitly annotated as still below nominal.
Adjacent prose states the failure implication and names the next comparison procedures.
item_reviews.summary: A clear failure-result page with interpretable evidence and an adjacent diagnostic conclusion.

observations: Input, GT, Prediction, and Error panels visibly depict the same annular case.
The error panel contains a highlighted ROI, with a connector leading to same-case GT, prediction, and error zoom crops.
The adjacent overlay legend clearly identifies TP, FP, and FN colors.
item_reviews.summary: Same-case full panels, ROI zooms, and the TP/FP/FN legend make the segmentation error interpretable.

observations: The flow visibly connects observed high-ICC coverage shortfall to sampling manipulations, comparator arms, and a go/no-go rule.
Sampling alternatives and comparator methods are named rather than left as generic placeholders.
The decision criterion specifies coverage threshold and controlled-width condition, with a stated no-go stratification action.
item_reviews.summary: A concrete evidence-to-decision next-experiment plan rather than generic future-work content.
